entities.summary:
Duke University, founded in 1838 in Durham, North Carolina, as Trinity College and renamed Duke University in 1924 following a massive endowment from James Buchanan Duke's tobacco fortune, is one of America's leading research universities known for its medical school, law school, and Nicholas School of the Environment. Duke's transformation from a small Methodist college to a major research university in the 20th century was the most dramatic institutional metamorphosis in American higher education history.

James B. Duke's $40 million endowment (1924) — equivalent to over $700 million today — funded the construction of Duke's Gothic West Campus in Durham stone and the transformation of Trinity College into Duke University. The American Tobacco Company fortune that funded Duke also funds the Duke Endowment, one of America's major philanthropic foundations. The university's medical center (Duke University Hospital), founded in 1930, became one of America's leading academic medical centers, serving the economically deprived rural South where medical care was scarce.

Duke's Nicholas School of the Environment and its marine lab at Beaufort, North Carolina, pioneered American environmental education. Duke's primate research center (DPC) at the Duke Forest houses the world's largest collection of lemurs outside Madagascar. Duke's basketball program — under Coach K Mike Krzyzewski — is among the most successful in college sports, with five NCAA championships and national cultural significance.
